; epp512.txt
;
; This is a disassembly of epp512.exe with my annotations
;
;  Tom Trebisky  10-22-2026
;
; Most of the annotation is further down in the file
; The netwide (dis)assembler was used -- see the Makefile

; -----------------------------------------------------------

; Studying disassembled code like this provides an endless
;  source of addictive puzzles.  A little routine will
;  pop up that calls no other routine and does something
;  with its inputs.  What is it doing?
;
; Apart from getting distracted by things like this, the
;   purpose of studying this is to understand the
;   algorithms used to read and particularly program
;   EPROM devices.

; -----------------------------------------------------------
;
; According to some notes from the MOD-EMUP over USB project,
; all software checks the EMUP in the following way:
;   It writes 00, 01, 00, 02 and then pulses to register E7
;   then it reads the low nibble of register F8.
;   (which the ALL-03 documentation doesn't mention)
; The app doesn't need it, but it shows there's logic in the
;   box we don't fully understand. See dosbox-x/README.md.
; They call this "The identification check."
; They learned all this by running the software in a patched
;  dosbox that logged each IO port access.
;
; by searching for 0xf8 I located this code.
; It is at 0xa66b
;
; This code also monkeys with 0xf7, which I don't see described.
;
; ------------------------------------------------
;
; There is a routine to set the VHH dac, but it is never called.
;  This implies that this program includes a shared block of code
;  that all of the EMUP gang of programs includes.
; If this is true, it may be possible to identify this block of code
;   in other programs and greatly simplify their analysis

; ------------------------------------------------
;
; You will note lines with a comment like the following:
;
;   call 0xd974   ;0x9b2:0x3e54
;
; This is done by my "fixadd" script.
; These are "far" calls and the cs:ip notation is all
;  but useless -- so I convert it to a flat address so
;  this code can be studied.   The original was like so:
;
;   call 0x16f:0x2690
;
; This same issue comes up in other places (data references)
;  that I didn't fix, and they are a pain to sort out.
; Often the ds register is loaded in one place and then
;  another register (typically bx) is used subsequently
;
; ------------------------------------------
; We don't start here at address 0
; The start is at 0x3da4 (given in the EXE header)
;
; This code at zero is just a subroutine called from below.
; I call this "zerosub"

; We end up here with CS = 07e8 and DS=ES=SS = 17a6

zerosub:
    0x0  0x0:0x0        55                push bp
    0x1  0x0:0x1        8BEC              mov bp,sp

; PORTS
; locations 365c and 3660 hold port numbers used
;  to talk to the EMUP
; There are only 2 ports!
;  3660 will hold 0x2E0 - the write only "ID" port
;  365c will hold 0x2E2 - the read/write "DATA" port

; Here we are setting those values.
; If   3660 gets 0x2E0
; then 365c gets 0x2E2
;
; port at 3660 gets only the following values written:
; e0 e1 e2 e3 e4 -- e8 eb

  0x19b  0x0:0x19b      A1A831            mov ax,[0x31a8]

  0x1a4  0x0:0x1a4      050200            add ax,0x2
  0x1a7  0x0:0x1a7      A35C36            mov [0x365c],ax		; save as EMUP "DATA" port

;
